messages:
Maya Patel: Quick pulse — PR #9832 is blocked on architecture + RFC anchor. Can someone please paste the RFC link and confirm SLO delta? Need to merge before tomorrow's release window.
Alex Chen: RFC link: https://redwood.infra/rfcs/tiling-cache-2026.md — I added a short summary to the PR description.
Maya Patel: thanks! cc @Sandeep Rao for perf/SLO review.
Sandeep Rao: looking now. rough question — what's peak qps for the affected routes and the extra work per request?
Maya Patel: peak ~1200 qps (daytime ~800). This change adds one extra prefix lookup (KV) per request when cache miss occurs.
Sandeep Rao: ok quick calc coming in a sec.
Sandeep Rao: quick calc:
```text
extra latency = 0.9ms per req
95th latency delta ~= 0.9ms * 1.05 = ~0.95ms
SLO impact = 0.95 / 150ms * 100 = ~0.63%
```
Sandeep Rao: so SLO delta ~0.6% — acceptable for standard tier, but for enterprise SLAs we should route traffic to fallback during rollout.
Megan Liu: canary plan suggestion: 30m window in us-west-2. ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback if errors >1% or p95 regresses >2ms.
Alex Chen: added the RFC link and perf numbers to PR description: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9832
Maya Patel: thanks. @Chris Park can you give an arch ack? Need explicit signoff to remove merge hold.
Chris Park: skimmed the RFC + PR — lgtm with the canary plan + SLO calc. please add a short ops runbook step about evicting stale prefetched entries and a healthcheck for prefetched cache size.
Maya Patel: will add the runbook line and healthcheck note to the PR. removing hold now — plan to merge after CI passes. :tada:
ci-bot: Build passed on main — all checks green.
Maya Patel: merging in 5m unless anyone objects.
Sandeep Rao: no objections. :+1:
Maya Patel: merged. thanks everyone.
